title: wrapture workshops
description: Guided JupyterLab workshops that teach wrapture: wrapping call sites without changing the code being observed, for monkey patching, testing and tracing.

workshops.name: first-binding
workshops.title: Your first binding
workshops.description: Create a wrapture binding on a method, apply and remove it, and change what a call does while the real code keeps running.

workshops.name: wrap-not-replace
workshops.title: Testing by wrapping, not replacing
workshops.description: Write the same unit tests with unittest.mock and with wrapture, and see what a test can say when the real code keeps running. Strict stubs, calls an object makes to itself, one thing changed, and what did not happen.

workshops.name: recording-calls
workshops.title: Recording what real code did
workshops.description: Record real calls on a timeline and read the tape back. Find a connection leak that no return value reveals, name the method and the line that leaked it, and turn the record into a pytest test that fails until you fix the code.

workshops.name: phased-behaviour
workshops.title: Behaviour that changes over time
workshops.description: Test retry logic, a circuit breaker and a polling loop with phases, where a binding's behaviour changes on a count, on a condition, when a sequence runs out, or on a signal from another binding.

workshops.name: beyond-callables
workshops.title: Bindings that are not calls
workshops.description: Watch and guard an attribute's reads and writes, hold a value in an environment variable or a module constant, pin the content of a settings dict for every holder, wrap a callable kept in a registry, and see how far a consumer read a generator.

workshops.name: live-tracing
workshops.title: A program that narrates itself
workshops.description: Apply bindings in a program's entry point, with no timeline, and register a sink that prints each call as it happens. Keep card numbers out of the trace, then narrow it at the sink, at the binding, and for a whole subtree, and read the count of what was left out.

workshops.name: zero-code-tracing
workshops.title: Tracing without touching the program
workshops.description: Move the bindings and the sink out of the program into a wrapture.toml beside it and run the program unchanged, under the runner and then injected at interpreter startup. Ask a traced process what is installed and switch it off and on, keep the trace as JSON Lines, read it back, and draw it as a sequence diagram.

workshops.name: analysing-a-trace
workshops.title: Analysing a trace in a notebook
workshops.description: A JSON Lines trace is data. Run the shop for three hundred orders under a file sink, read the file into a DataFrame, rebuild the tree from the parent links, work out where the time and the errors went, chart the latency of an order by tenant, and draw a few orders as a sequence diagram and a diff.

workshops.name: tracing-flask
workshops.title: One request as one tree
workshops.description: Put the shop behind Flask and record each HTTP request as one tree, with the view and the shop's own methods nested beneath it, from a single instrument entry in the config. Send a quote, an order, a declined order and a request that fails with a 500, read the trees, then keep the health checks out.

workshops.name: finding-slow-code
workshops.title: Where the time goes
workshops.description: The order endpoint of the Flask shop is slow. Read the time off one request's tree, tell slow itself from slow because of a child with self time, turn that into a test that asserts on it, get one report for thirty requests from an Aggregate window in the config, and tag each request with the tenant it was for.
